definition: Optical fiber is a thin transparent strand that guides light along its length for communication or sensing.
example: A fiber transmits light pulses carrying data between network transceivers.

definition: Optical waveguides are structures that confine and direct light along a defined path.
example: A photonic chip sends light between its components through a patterned waveguide.

definition: Oral hygiene consists of practices that keep the mouth clean and help prevent dental and gum disease.
example: A person cleans between their teeth to remove plaque missed by brushing.

definition: Order of draw is the recommended sequence for collecting blood into different specimen tubes to minimize additive carryover.
example: A phlebotomist consults the laboratory's order-of-draw chart before collecting several specimens.

definition: The organic composition of capital is Marx's concept for the ratio of constant to variable capital insofar as that ratio reflects the technical relationship between means of production and labor power.
example: A political economist uses the concept to examine how mechanization changes the relationship between expenditures on machinery and labor.

definition: Organization development applies planned, evidence-informed interventions to improve how an organization functions and adapts.
example: A facilitator helps several departments diagnose recurring coordination problems and test a new workflow.

definition: Organizational change is the process by which an organization alters its structure, practices, strategy or culture.
example: A company changes reporting lines and introduces new routines after combining two teams.

definition: Outbound logistics manages the storage, handling and transport of goods from an organization to customers or distribution channels.
example: A retailer consolidates customer orders before dispatching them from a fulfillment center.

definition: Outpatient surgery is planned to allow the patient to leave without an overnight hospital stay when recovery permits.
example: A surgical center schedules a follow-up after a patient goes home on the day of the procedure.

definition: An overhead camshaft engine places one or more camshafts in the cylinder head to operate the valves.
example: An automotive student compares how single- and dual-overhead-cam layouts actuate valves.

definition: An overhead valve engine places its valves in the cylinder head and, in common automotive usage, operates them with pushrods from a camshaft in the block.
example: A mechanic identifies a pushrod engine by inspecting the linkage that opens its valves.

definition: Oxidation processes involve loss of electrons or an increase in oxidation state, sometimes through reaction with oxygen.
example: Iron loses electrons as its surface corrodes.

definition: Pandemic preparedness is advance planning and capacity building to detect and respond to widespread outbreaks.
example: A public health agency exercises its plan for sharing alerts and maintaining essential services.

definition: The parasympathetic nervous system is the autonomic division that supports functions such as slowing the heart and promoting digestion.
example: A physiology student explains how parasympathetic activity helps reduce heart rate during rest.

definition: The Paris Agreement is an international climate treaty that organizes collective action through national commitments, reporting and periodic review.
example: A country submits a revised nationally determined contribution describing its emissions goals.

definition: Partnership taxation concerns how tax rules apply to a partnership and how its income, losses and other items are allocated to partners.
example: An accountant checks whether each partner's allocated income matches the applicable partnership agreement and reporting rules.

definition: The path to purchase describes the interactions and decisions a buyer goes through before completing a purchase.
example: A retailer examines how product reviews and store visits influence a buyer's final choice.

definition: Pathology informatics applies information systems and data methods to diagnostic pathology and laboratory workflows.
example: A pathology service routes a scanned slide to the correct case in its reporting system.

definition: Patient identification and matching links records and care events to the correct individual using identifying attributes and verification procedures.
example: A clinic checks for duplicate records when two entries have similar names and dates of birth.

definition: Pediatric surgery is the specialty concerned with surgical care of infants, children and adolescents.
example: A pediatric surgical team adapts perioperative planning to a young patient's size and development.

definition: The pelvic floor is a group of muscles and connective tissues that supports pelvic organs and contributes to continence and other functions.
example: A physiotherapist diagrams how the pelvic floor supports the bladder.

definition: Pelvic health concerns the function and well-being of the pelvic organs and supporting structures.
example: A clinician evaluates whether a pelvic floor disorder is contributing to a patient's symptoms.

definition: Penology studies punishment, correctional institutions and approaches to rehabilitation or reintegration.
example: A researcher compares outcomes of community supervision and incarceration for similar cases.

definition: Perinatology is the medical specialty concerned with high-risk pregnancy and the health of the pregnant patient and fetus around birth.
example: A maternal-fetal medicine specialist monitors a pregnancy complicated by fetal growth concerns.

definition: Perioperative care encompasses the preparation, support and monitoring provided before, during and after surgery.
example: A care team verifies a patient's readiness for surgery and monitors recovery afterwards.

definition: Personal Communications Service refers to mobile wireless voice and data services designated as PCS in telecommunications regulation.
example: A carrier operates cellular service in a licensed PCS band.
sense_note: The frequencies and regulatory scope depend on jurisdiction.

definition: Personal income tax is a tax assessed on an individual's taxable income under applicable rules.
example: A taxpayer separates taxable wages from qualifying deductions when preparing a return.

definition: Pet insurance is coverage that reimburses or pays eligible veterinary or related expenses under a policy.
example: An owner submits a claim for a covered veterinary visit after a pet is injured.

definition: Petrography describes and classifies rocks through close observation of their mineral composition and texture, commonly in thin section.
example: A geologist examines a thin rock slice under polarized light to identify its constituent minerals.

definition: Pharmacogenetics studies how inherited genetic differences influence individual responses to medications.
example: Researchers examine whether variation in one gene changes how quickly patients break down a medication.

definition: Pharmacoinformatics applies computational and information methods to data about drugs and their discovery, use or effects.
example: A researcher integrates drug and target records to compare known interactions.
sense_note: Usage spans drug-discovery and clinical-information contexts.

definition: Philosophy of religion examines concepts and arguments concerning religion, such as faith, divinity and religious experience.
example: A seminar evaluates whether a proposed account of faith requires evidence.

definition: Philosophy of science studies the concepts, methods and assumptions behind scientific inquiry and explanation.
example: A researcher compares how two philosophical accounts distinguish causal explanations from predictions.

definition: PHP frameworks provide reusable libraries and conventions for building PHP applications.
example: A developer uses a framework's routing and request-validation features to build a form service.

definition: Physical security protects people, facilities and physical assets from unauthorized access, damage and other threats.
example: A laboratory uses controlled entry and visitor records to protect secure workspaces.

definition: Plastic surgery is a surgical specialty focused on restoring or reshaping structures of the body for reconstructive or aesthetic purposes.
example: A surgical team reconstructs an area of tissue affected by an injury.

definition: Platform as a service provides a managed environment for developing and running applications without administering the underlying infrastructure.
example: A team deploys an application to a managed runtime without setting up its own servers.

definition: Police accountability comprises mechanisms that require law enforcement agencies and personnel to explain their actions, undergo oversight and address misconduct.
example: An oversight body reviews complaints and publishes findings about recurring procedural problems.

definition: The price-to-book ratio compares a company's market equity value with its accounting book value of equity.
example: An analyst compares the ratios of two banks with similar accounting practices.

definition: Prisoners' rights are legal protections that people retain while incarcerated.
example: An advocate examines whether a prison's access-to-care practices meet applicable legal standards.
sense_note: Specific protections and remedies depend on jurisdiction.
